questions.q: Which gate is a fixed, deterministic bit-flip with no adjustable parameter?
options: qc.rx(theta, 0)
qc.h(0)
qc.x(0)
qc.s(0)
questions.explain: qc.x(0) applies the Pauli-X gate, which deterministically flips |0> to |1> and vice versa, with no angle parameter involved.

questions.q: What exact statevector does qc.h(0) produce starting from |0>?
questions.explain: The Hadamard gate applied to |0> produces the |+> state, with equal real amplitudes of 0.7071068 on both |0> and |1>.

options: A sampled measurement result from running shots on a simulator
The exact complex amplitudes of the circuit's state, with no sampling involved
The circuit's depth and qubit count
A noisy approximation of the final state
questions.explain: Statevector(qc) returns the ideal, exact mathematical amplitudes for every basis state — it's a direct calculation, not a statistical sample.

questions.q: qc.rx(math.pi/2, 0) applied to |0> gives statevector [0.7071068+0j, 0-0.7071068j], with the same measurement probabilities as qc.h(0)'s [0.7071068+0j, 0.7071068+0j]. Why are these not the same quantum state?
options: They actually are the same state — the difference is a typo
The second has a different probability of measuring 1
The second amplitude carries an imaginary relative phase, which changes the physical state even though squared magnitude (and so measurement probability) is unaffected
RX only works on multi-qubit circuits
questions.explain: Measurement probability depends only on squared magnitude of an amplitude, and |0.7071068|^2 equals |-0.7071068j|^2. But the relative phase between amplitudes is physically real and affects how the state behaves under further gates, even though one measurement right now can't distinguish it.

questions.q: What distinguishes the rotation gates RX, RY, RZ from the fixed gates X, Y, Z?
options: Rotation gates only work on 2+ qubit circuits
Rotation gates take an explicit angle argument, letting you rotate by any amount instead of a fixed operation
Fixed gates cannot be used before measurement
Rotation gates always produce deterministic outcomes
questions.explain: RX, RY, and RZ accept an angle in radians as a parameter, allowing continuous, tunable rotation — this is what makes them central to variational algorithms later in the course.
